target.population: Mexico analytical-use design: adults aged 25-79 with no reported prior doctor diagnosis of diabetes/high blood sugar, recorded 8-12-hour fast, positive fasting serum glucose below 126 mg/dL, available HbA1c and valid standing anthropometry with internally consistent measurement documentation (uniformly excluding explicit not-weighed or alternative-standing-route documentation that contradicts usable standing measurements, without asserting which field is correct) under the prespecified measurement restrictions; pregnancy/lactation excluded when documented by questionnaire routing for women aged 25-49; no verified medication or anemia exclusion. Exactly 250 fictional individuals per female=0/1 crossed with age bands 25-39, 40-54, 55-69, 70-79; equal-stratum analytical design, not a nationally representative population.

lifelines.population: Lifelines western-European unrelated adults selected for GWAS, oldest family members preferred; n=2921 eligible; excludes self-reported diabetes or FPG>=7.0 mmol/L, significant anemia, and missing HbA1c/erythrocytes/FPG. Table 2 row-specific n unknown; Table 3 complete-case n unresolved. Approximate reconstruction with assumed integer age support 18-95 and a discretized Gaussian age distribution; no source individual data.

pani.population: Pani NHANES 2001-2004 n=3270, adults age>=25, no self-reported diabetes, FPG<126 mg/dL, HbA1c available. Complex survey design and weights. FOS context is different and is not pooled. NHANES overlaps Liu1999-2008. Approximate reconstruction with age-band probabilities proportional to unweighted counts, uniform integer ages below 70, and an assumed declining 70-95 tail; no source individual data or recovered survey weights.

assumptions.description: Common computational age domain is integer 18-95, female is 0/1, BMI and HbA1c are positive and glucose is positive and below 126 mg/dL. This domain covers all three contexts; it is not an observed clinical range. Target age remains 25-79. Source age supports are author assumptions.

Target has exactly 250 rows in each female 0/1 by age-band 25-39,40-54,55-69,70-79 intersection, with integer ages uniform within each band. Quotas are supplied analytical design; within-band uniformity is assumed. No prevalence or national representativeness follows.

Lifelines explicit age limits are unknown. Approximate adult age mass is proportional to exp(-0.5*((age-55.5)/9.9)^2) on integer 18-95, independently of female. The endpoints are modeling bounds, not extracted source facts; truncation and discretization slightly change published moments.

Pani age-band mass is proportional to the eight published unweighted sample counts, although published means used survey weights. Integer ages are uniform in each closed band below 70. The open final band is approximated by ages 70-95 with mass exp(-(age-70)/7); 95 and decay scale 7 are assumptions. This includes ages beyond the target 79 ceiling but leaves unmodeled the true far-oldest tail and weighted age distribution.

Lifelines female probability is the complement 0.597 of rounded male proportion 0.403; this does not decode a regression sex coefficient. Pani female probability is assumed 0.5 because its source composition was not supplied. Age and female are independent in source approximations; target follows quotas.

At the Lifelines age/female reference, conditional BMI and fasting glucose locations equal reported means. Assumed BMI age slope 0.025 kg/m^2/year and female contrast +0.6 kg/m^2, glucose age slope +0.10 mg/dL/year and female contrast -1.5 mg/dL. These modest slopes are structural choices, not recovered source estimates. They are constant across all contexts.

Conditional BMI/glucose residuals have a bivariate normal distribution with correlation 0.30 independent of age and female. This unreported covariance closes two separate Jansen projections into one joint conditional HbA1c equation; it is not identified by the evidence. Normal BMI tails, linear dependence and homoskedasticity are approximations.

All contexts are generated directly as selected analytical populations. Conditional BMI/glucose pairs are redrawn until BMI>0 and 0<glucose<126, holding age and female fixed. This is an assumed selected-distribution approximation, not a mechanistic disease/diagnosis/fasting/anthropometry eligibility model. Threshold conditioning slightly changes marginal moments and projection algebra.

HbA1c has one linear conditional rule in age, BMI and glucose, a zero direct female contrast, and independent Gaussian residuals truncated only at positivity. Zero direct female effect is an explicit assumption, not an inference from missing source coefficients. Jansen total percent SD 0.3 is decomposed using assumed covariance and Pani age slope. No interactions, saturation or age-varying residual scale are identified.

Pani location is the count-weighted average of the eight reported survey age-band HbA1c means, anchored at the expected age of the assumed Pani age distribution and female probability 0.5. Mixing survey band means with unweighted counts is approximate and is not a recovered national mean. The band means constrain this one location; they are not eight independently fitted intercepts. The common linear model may disagree with their older-age plateau.

Jansen age/sex-adjusted BMI and glucose projection coefficients are converted to conditional coefficients only after declaring residual BMI/glucose covariance; Pani age coefficient adjusted for female/BMI/glucose is then imposed as the shared conditional age coefficient. Assuming these cross-cohort coefficients coexist in one linear law is an unverified scientific synthesis, not an identified joint regression.

Target adopts exactly the Pani HbA1c location rule and the common Lifelines-based BMI/glucose locations, scales, trends, dependence and residual law. No ethnicity-specific or Mexico-specific correction is supplied or estimated. Transport from western-European Lifelines and US NHANES to Mexican adults is unverified, including ancestry, nutrition, adiposity, age selection and socioeconomic differences.

All outputs use task units; glucose conversion is fixed 18.0 mg/dL per mmol/L and HbA1c projection conversion uses 0.09148 without offset. Source feedback is identity mapping after conversion in admitted evidence. Applying fasting-plasma relationships to target fasting serum assumes no systematic plasma/serum bias, no fasting-duration effect within the target 8-12 hours, and sufficient assay comparability; these are not established by unit conversion.

Lifelines excluded significant anemia; the target has no verified anemia or medication exclusion. No latent anemia, medication, pregnancy or lactation effect is separately identified; their net conditional effect is assumed covered by the transported residual/location. Target pregnancy/lactation exclusion applies only when documented for routed women 25-49; older unasked status remains unresolved. This model cannot verify eligibility or resolve anthropometric documentation.

Pani feedback uses ordinary Monte Carlo sample means and OLS with intercept, preserving the printed adjustment set and units. It does not reconstruct complex-survey weights, strata or clusters; source row composition and estimator are approximations. Reported SEs remain sampling uncertainty and never become individual SDs.

Fixed source estimates and assumed parameters define one initial scenario. Gaussian individual variation and seed variation are not evidence/model/transport uncertainty. Unknown Jansen interval confidence levels and coefficient SEs preclude a justified parameter posterior; no probability distribution over scientific assumptions is claimed.

Only the controller executes generation. Random draws use the passed seed, no external files/data/network. A finite rejection-attempt guard raises an error rather than silently clipping values; output is not locally smoke-tested by the builder.

active_context.derivation: Selector only; the bridge changes this key and no scientific setting.

contexts.derivation: Task descriptor is copied exactly. Lifelines source age/sex distribution uses Table 1 marginal evidence. Pani band counts are the supplied Table 1 unweighted counts; tail and within-band ages are assumptions. Source tasks contain 6000 Monte Carlo rows. Target selects exactly the Pani HbA1c reference, while common covariate parameters remain unchanged.

lifelines_reference.derivation: Jansen Table 1 printed percent HbA1c mean/SD 5.6/0.3; no use of the rounded alternate IFCC marginal. FPG 5.1/0.5 mmol/L becomes 91.8/9.0 mg/dL using 18.0. Female 0.597 is 1-0.403. Marginal moments do not identify a joint law.

covariate_trends.derivation: Four assumed conditional age and female associations, shared across all populations; none is a recovered scientific coefficient.

conditional_residual_correlation.derivation: Residual BMI/glucose Pearson correlation 0.30 is an explicit closure assumption; not extracted or fitted to generated data.

reported_projection_constraints.derivation: Preserves two separate Jansen age/female-adjusted projections and the Pani female/BMI/glucose-adjusted age coefficient. Jansen slopes use NGSP multiplier and glucose factor only; no Liu or Table 3 calibration.

conditional_coefficients.derivation: Analytical, pre-truncation construction: sB^2=SD_B^2-bA^2*SD_A^2-bF^2*pF*(1-pF), likewise sG. Given r=0.30, betaB=(qB-qG*r*sG/sB)/(1-r^2), betaG=(qG-qB*r*sB/sG)/(1-r^2). Thus the separate age/female-adjusted projection equations are qB=betaB+betaG*r*sG/sB and qG=betaG+betaB*r*sB/sG, rather than concatenating qB and qG. betaAge=0.010. Independent HbA1c residual variance is 0.3^2 minus variance of the linear signal under assumed Lifelines age/sex moments. Gaussian truncation and finite age approximation make all source equalities approximate.

hba1c_references.derivation: Lifelines level 5.6 is anchored at age55.5/female probability0.597. Pani level=sum(unweighted band n*reported survey band mean)/3270, anchored at the count-weighted expected age under declared within-band age laws and assumed female probability0.5. Target reuses precisely this Pani anchor. This aggregate operation does not identify a survey-weighted overall mean or fit eight individual age curves.

max_rejection_rounds.derivation: Computational guard only, no clipping or numerical fallback on failure.
